messages:
anya: FYI rolling out driver 536.x in us-west2 caused a spike of PTX link failures on a subset of H100 Hopper SM90 nodes. seeing compile/link errors and intermittent NCCL stalls.

cj: can you paste a short log sample?

anya: sure, here's a cut from one of the affected pods:
```
[2024-06-02T09:12:05Z] device 0: ptx_link error: unresolved symbol: __nv_builtin_truncf
[2024-06-02T09:12:05Z] ptxas: relocation overflow at 0x7f9a1b2c
runtime: kernel compile failed -> falling back to interpreter path
```

mike: same pattern as the eu canary last week but rates higher in west. throughput dips ~10-30% on worst nodes, tail-latency up. NCCL shows short collective stalls (several hundred ms) not full disconnects.

navdeep: initial correlation: affected nodes are running distro kernel 5.15 + driver 536.x. nodes with 6.x kernels + same driver are largely green. maybe a kernel toolchain/ptx ABI mismatch.

samira: did we change base AMI or compiler flags in the new image? any different nvcc/ptxas versions baked into container layers?

anya: containers look same; suspect the kernel+driver combo changed behavior. repro steps we used on an affected host:
```
# quick smoke
docker run --gpus all --rm nvcr.io/nvidia/pytorch:24.08 bash -lc "python -c 'import torch; torch.randn(2, device=\"cuda\")'"
# then run small attn kernel job and check dmesg for ptx entries
dmesg | grep -i ptx
```

infra-bot: Canary metrics (us-west2/hopper-pool-5): error-rate +2.4%, tail-latency +22%, throughput -14% since 2024-06-02T08:55Z.

cj: mitigation options?

navdeep: options:
- rollback driver on affected subset to 535.61 (fastest)
- rebuild AMI with kernel 6.x and migrate (safer long-term but longer lead)
- serve pinned CUBIN artifacts for vulnerable runtimes if we have them cached
- temporarily pin workloads to non-H100 pools where possible

mike: rollback is lowest risk. we can cordon bad nodes, move low-priority jobs first, canary rollback 3 nodes, observe 30m. if good, batch roll remaining.

samira: starting cordon on hopper-5c02, moving ~10 pods (low-priority) now. ETA 6m. autoscaler will spawn replacements; expect short capacity spike. tagging cost_center=inference-ops.

anya: plan: 1) cordon high-error nodes (anya) 2) spawn 3-node rollback canary (navdeep) 3) monitor metrics 30m (cj) 4) if stable, roll remaining affected nodes at 10% per wave with 15m windows (samira) 5) open NV ticket with ptx dump + dmesg (mike).

navdeep: canary started at 2024-06-02T09:25Z on hopper-5c07 with driver 535.61 deployed. collecting ptxas/nvcc and kernel build-id across hosts.

mike: opened ENG-NVIDIA ticket #24877 with attached logs, ptx snippets, and canary traces. CC: @anya @navdeep.

navdeep: quick diagnostic job to collect versions (will push across fleets):
```
#!/bin/bash
for host in $(cat hostlist); do
 ssh $host "uname -r; cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version; nvcc --version 2>/dev/null || true; ptxas --version 2>/dev/null || true"
done
```

cj: cost impact note: moving workloads and reduced throughput will increase hourly GPU consumption by ~6-9% and unit token cost ~5% if this persists >8h. loop in finance if rollout extends.

samira: canary results: after 28m driver rollback -> 0 PTX link errors on canary nodes, NCCL stalls returned to baseline. initiating controlled roll at 10% waves.

anya: added temporary runbook step to eng-oncall: if PTX link errors >0.5% for 10m, cordon pool, run canary rollback, file NV ticket.

navdeep: follow-ups:
- collect full ptx/ptxas differences and map to kernel toolchain versions (navdeep)
- add PTX/linking tests to our preflight canary matrix and CI for H100 SM90 (cj)
- create a small job to validate CUBIN fallback artifacts and cache them in S3 (mike)
- estimate customer impact and craft comms if >4h (samira)

mike: reminder: some long-running jobs will reload KV-cache on move (10-45s). prefer moving low-priority first.

anya: postmortem owner: @navdeep. suspected root cause: PTX codegen differences triggered by kernel toolchain + newer driver expecting additional builtin symbols. NV will confirm.

infra-bot: rollback completed for affected subset at 2024-06-02T11:10Z. metrics show recovery.

cj: once postmortem is ready, add recommended AMI/kernel/driver matrix to docs and preflight gating. closing this thread but will keep updates in incident channel.

anya: thanks everyone. will reopen if similar behavior shows up in other regions.
